# Opencode Provider Mistral-Vibe Adds [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe) to [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) as a model provider, so your coding agent runs on the models your Vibe plan already pays for and not on a pay-per-token API key. Based on the original idea of [opencode-with-vibe](https://github.com/ilyhalight/opencode-with-vibe). Every model request is executed by a small local Python bridge that uses Vibe's own completion adapter, model configuration and OIDC credential. In practice that means: - **Billed to your Vibe plan.** Completions carry the same client metadata the `vibe` CLI sends, so Mistral meters them against your workspace balance / abo credits instead of a raw API budget. - **Your account's models.** The plugin loads Vibe's curated online catalog for your account - including third-party models Mistral hosts for Vibe - and contributes them to `/models` with real per-model costs. - **Native agent behavior.** Text and reasoning stream live, tool calls return to OpenCode for execution, and token/cache usage is reported per request. - **Zero manual setup.** If no compatible Vibe runtime is installed, the plugin installs its own pinned copy automatically and never touches anything you already have. - **Errors say what happened.** Quota, auth, network and version failures surface with their real cause - including an observed network diagnostic when you are offline - never a generic "run setup" mask. ## Quick start On the machine running the OpenCode server: ```sh # from the GitHub repository opencode plugin add "github:AiPrimitivesStudio/Opencode-Provider-Mistral-Vibe#main::path:package" # or from npm opencode plugin add @aiprimitivesstudio/opencode-mistral-vibe ``` Then, inside OpenCode: 1. `/connect` -> **Mistral Vibe** -> **Use Vibe login**. If you already use the `vibe` CLI and are logged in, you are done: pick a model in `/models`. 2. An OpenCode-only machine has no credentials yet - the login command is not executed by OpenCode; run it once from a terminal, exactly as the connection status names it (the plugin-managed `vibe` binary), e.g.: ```sh # Windows "%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\mistral-vibe-runtime\\Scripts\vibe.exe" --setup # macOS / Linux ~/.config/opencode/mistral-vibe-runtime//bin/vibe --setup ``` It opens a browser to sign in to Mistral and stores the credential once in `~/.vibe` (shared with the `vibe` CLI, should you ever install it). 3. Pick a model in `/models`, for example `mistral-vibe/mistral-medium-3.5#high`, and start prompting. Credentials are read at request time, so models work immediately after the login - no reconnect needed. The connection badge may still read not-logged-in until the next refresh; reconnecting once simply clears it sooner. On a machine with no Vibe at all, the plugin installs its pinned runtime in the background on first load - give that a moment; the login command in step 2 only exists once that install has finished (the connection status names it from then on). Pin a version by pointing at a tag instead of the branch: ```sh opencode plugin add "github:AiPrimitivesStudio/Opencode-Provider-Mistral-Vibe#v0.1.0::path:package" ``` Or ride the newest release instead of the branch: ```sh opencode plugin add "github:AiPrimitivesStudio/Opencode-Provider-Mistral-Vibe#latest::path:package" ``` The `latest` tag moves with every release. A tag install stays on the version it resolved until you run `opencode plugin update`; `#main` follows the branch instead. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TB OC["OpenCode
session, tools, history, approvals"] subgraph PLUGIN["mistral-vibe plugin - TypeScript"] IDX["index.ts
provider, models, costs"] MODEL["model.ts
AI SDK adapter"] PROC["process.ts
bridge lifecycle"] RT["runtime.ts
runtime bootstrap"] end subgraph BRIDGE["Python bridge - one short-lived process per request"] B["bridge.py
NDJSON over stdio"] end subgraph VIBE["Vibe runtime - pinned mistral-vibe"] CFG["orchestrator
+ user model config"] OIDC["OIDC credential
resolution"] ADAPTER["Vibe's Mistral
completion adapter"] end KEYS[("~/.vibe
shared login store")] API["Mistral API
billed to the Vibe plan"] OC -->|"model request"| MODEL MODEL --> PROC IDX -.->|"catalog probe on connect and reload"| PROC RT -->|"pinned runtime if nothing compatible"| PROC PROC -->|"spawn"| B B --> CFG B --> OIDC B --> ADAPTER OIDC --> KEYS ADAPTER -->|"HTTPS, vibe_code client metadata"| API API -.->|"streamed deltas, tool calls, usage"| B B -->|"events"| PROC PROC --> MODEL MODEL --> OC ``` Every request crosses the plugin as one Python process speaking NDJSON over stdio: OpenCode keeps ownership of the agent loop, Vibe keeps ownership of transport and credentials, and the only thing that leaves the machine is the HTTPS call Mistral's own Vibe adapter makes - metered against your plan. ## Non-standard setups ### Runtime resolution and the bootstrap The plugin speaks Vibe's internal Python adapter API, so it is deliberately **pinned to one tested runtime version** - never floating. The pin lives in a single source constant (`REQUIRED_VIBE_VERSION` in `package/src/runtime.ts`); the managed runtime, the automatic install and the compatibility gate all derive from it, and a runtime outside the pinned line fails with an explicit error naming the version it needs instead of guessing. At startup it picks a runtime in this order: 1. `OPENCODE_VIBE_PYTHON` - an explicit interpreter path, used as-is; 2. the plugin-managed runtime it installed itself (`~/.config/opencode/mistral-vibe-runtime//`); 3. any Vibe you already have - **but only if its version is on the pinned runtime's line**. If nothing compatible exists, the plugin installs its own pinned copy in the background: atomically (temp dir + swap), behind a cross-process lock, without ever upgrading, downgrading or otherwise touching a Vibe you already use. Your own tool keeps working for your CLI use, whatever version it runs; OpenCode uses its private pinned copy. Installs never block server startup, and a failed install surfaces its real cause. - `OPENCODE_VIBE_AUTO_INSTALL=0` - disable the bootstrap; the plugin then fails loudly instead of silently using an incompatible runtime. - `OPENCODE_VIBE_RUNTIME_DIR` - where the managed runtime lives. - `OPENCODE_VIBE_UV` / `OPENCODE_VIBE_BASE_PYTHON` - the `uv` binary (default: `uv` on PATH) and the fallback Python used to create the managed venv (`py` on Windows, `python3` elsewhere). `uv` is preferred when present. ### Paths and process behavior - `OPENCODE_VIBE_PATH` - path to a `vibe` launcher (otherwise PATH, then `~/.local/bin/vibe`). - `OPENCODE_VIBE_PREWARM=0` - start the Python bridge cold for every request. By default one idle bridge with Vibe already imported waits for the next model request (~0.6 s faster per request, ~85 MB of memory) and stops after 10 idle minutes. Each request still runs in its own process and reads configuration and credentials at request time. - `VIBE_HOME` - honored by Vibe for user configuration and authentication. Set these in the **server's environment**, not just the terminal client. ### Where models, billing and credentials actually go - OpenCode owns instructions, history, tools, approvals, compaction and subagents; the bridge runs exactly one model call per request - there is no second agent loop and no flattening of conversation history. - Credentials stay inside the Python process. Probe responses carry model metadata and an authentication-presence flag, never tokens; the crash-path traceback dump is redacted before it is written to disk. - Cancellation terminates only the bridge process belonging to that request. - Model requests carry Vibe's own client user-agent, so Mistral meters them like `vibe` CLI requests. ### Cost reporting Costs are reported from a maintained price table (`API_PRICES` in `package/src/index.ts`, official Mistral API rates per 1M tokens), because Vibe bills the workspace balance at exactly those rates. A blank cost in OpenCode means the model has no entry in the table yet - **not** free usage. ### Scope and limitations - Local-server integration; not registered in remote workspaces. - Lists Vibe's curated Mistral-hosted models and configured Mistral-backend models; generic third-party provider backends are not supported. - Supports text, reasoning, image input, function tools and token/cache usage. - Structured output and forced tool choice fail explicitly; unsupported sampling settings produce stream warnings; PDF/audio input is not supported. - Uses OpenCode's system prompt rather than Vibe's product prompt. - OpenCode HTTP hooks do not intercept Python's model requests. - Credential presence is checked locally; a successful paid model request still depends on account access. No sign-in is performed automatically. ### When something fails Errors are never masked. You will see the actual HTTP status, quota or auth error, and when OIDC credential resolution fails the plugin also reports what it observed on the network - for example: ``` OidcError: OIDC credential resolution failed; explicitly re-login (network check to api.mistral.ai:443 failed: gaierror [Errno 11001] getaddrinfo failed) ``` means the machine is offline; "network reachable" in the same message means the login store needs attention. Re-login always runs through the runtime actually serving requests (the no-credential message names the exact binary). ### Development and tests The installable package lives in `package/` (that is what `::path:package` points at). The in-repo layout: ``` package/ src/ TypeScript plugin + the Python bridge test/ unit (offline), bridge (real Vibe plan) and e2e suites ``` From this directory, with Node.js installed: ```sh cd package npm install npm run test:unit # offline gate; no API spend npm run typecheck npm run coverage:unit # offline c8 gate: >= 85% lines AND branches npm run coverage # full c8 gate (includes the token-spending suites) npm run test:e2e # spends real Vibe tokens ``` The unit suite is fully offline (a scripted fake bridge stands in for the real one; tests locate the Python interpreter from the uv tool layout, or set `OPENCODE_VIBE_PYTHON`). The e2e suites run the real bridge against the real Vibe plan - and one test sends a real message to the live OpenCode server (service URL and password from `~/.config/opencode/service.json`) - so they spend real tokens; run them only when you need that verification. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Vibe is installed separately and remains subject to its own license and service terms. Sources: [OpenCode plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), [OpenCode plugin API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/server/), [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe).
